Each pattern

1. Faint global overlay (watermark-like)

A regular ripple added to the pixel values over the whole frame with the same alignment everywhere, too faint to see, and not explained by JPEG blocks, pixel lattices or resizing. Invisible watermarks, electrical interference and scanner noise look like this.

How to read this

  • Every stripe width from 2 pixels up to a third of the image, in every direction, was tested in brightness and in both colour channels, 6 scans in all.
  • A pattern is reported only when it stands far above what the picture's own detail produces at neighbouring frequencies. "Strength" is that ratio.
  • "Whole frame" means the pattern has the same strength and alignment in every zone quiet enough to measure. Real subjects (fabric, fences) fail that test; overlays and processing pass it.
  • One image has limits: a very faint or very slow ripple can hide under busy detail, an exact 2× enlargement can leave no rhythm, and a cause is named from the pattern's geometry, which cannot prove who or what put it there.
